One should give sixteen parts of mercury together with one part of gold;
when the "fragrant elephant" (gandhanāga) has been digested, then the mercury becomes bound.
Once the gold has been digested, one should then color it with half as much of the processed metal (mṛtaloha). (Rasārṇava 11.93)
Copper killed with sulphur, along with pyrite, cinnabar, and iron, should be purified by means of a *puṭa* (herbivore) roast; one should then add six times as much pure gold. (Rasārṇava 11.94)

When the golden seed (*hemabīja*) has been digested four times during the *sūtaka* process, one should know that the mercury has acquired a fixed color (*baddharāga*); the mercury then becomes radiant like gold. (Rasārṇava 11.95)
One should cause it to flow together with that very [substance] while situated within a *sāraṇā* apparatus;
having performed the flowing for one-third part, one should again digest it in that very same place. (Rasārṇava 11.96)

By the application of the sevenfold chain-method (*saptaśṛṅkhalikāyoga*), mercury that has been heated (*jārita*) and circulated (*sārita*), and then again heated and circulated, becomes capable of piercing through a crore of layers. (Rasārṇava 11.97)
The alchemical process of *jāraṇā* pertaining to earth-dwellers has been explained; now hear about the *jāraṇā* of sky-dwellers.
One should have diamonds and other principal gems prepared as the residue of the liquid;
one should cause seeds of bitter gourd to be given with half that amount. (Rasārṇava 11.99)
The wise one should prepare a paste known as the "great liquefier" (mahājāraṇa) and place the mercury in the middle of it, at the mouth of the diamond-flask (vajramūṣā). Ras 11.100.
Having thus combined *kataka* and gold, one should grind them together;
then, with great care, one should cause a *grāsa* (bolus) of ruby (*padmarāga*) to be given into the liquid.

O Goddess of the Gods, when the redness of the mercury has matured during its impurity (*sūtaka*), it becomes eleven times [its original weight] and takes the form of a ruby (*padmarāga*) or a linga. 11.102.
It should be guarded with great effort by the eight guardians of the world (lokapālas), and one-sixth of the essence of the mercury (sūtaka) should be offered to all of them. (Rasārṇava 11.103)
Having bowed to the guru and the deities, and having paid homage to all the Siddhas and especially to the deities, one should consume [the substance] with great effort. (Rasārṇava 11.104)
From that, fainting and a burning sensation in the limbs arise; of this there is no doubt.
One should perceive oneself arisen, possessing divine luster and great strength. (Rasārṇava 11.105)
Accompanied by the sounds of conchs and trumpets, together with Siddhas and Vidyādharas,
he may travel through the worlds at will, assuming any form he desires and riding in a celestial chariot.
And where the gods dissolve, there the Siddha likewise dissolves.
Furthermore, I shall proclaim another supreme method for the process of digestion (jāraṇā). 11.108.
Then, having been well-rubbed, cooked, and processed, it is freed from all defects; [it is then treated] with the essence of leafy vegetables and the juice of *viṣṇukrāntā*. (Rasārṇava 11.109)
Sulfur treated with a decoction of *palāśa* flowers in equal parts, along with an equal amount of black mica essence and *rasaka*, becomes eightfold in its potency. (Rasakalpa 11.110)
One should digest even sharp and poisonous mercury using the tortoise apparatus (*kūrmayantra*);
thereafter, O Pārvatī, one should digest gold by means of a medicinal flux (*viḍayoga*). (Rasārṇava 11.111)

Then one should know that it is perfected; one should cause the copper to be divided into two parts according to the measure of the number of operations, whereby the lead becomes gold. (Rasārṇava 11.112)
Hereafter, I shall explain the supreme sequence of digestion (jāraṇā). (Rasārṇava 11.113)
Having repeatedly saturated the seed-powders with oil, one should slowly rub a morsel of them, equal to a sixteenth part, with the finger. (Rasārṇava 11.114)
Then, from the mixture beginning with ginger (ārdraka), it should be added in a sixteenth part;
having applied this to birch bark, it should then be placed in a swinging apparatus (dolāyantra). (Rasārṇava 11.115)
O Dear One, within a day and night, the *sūtaka* swallows that seed;
having extracted that mercury, O Goddess, one should then grind it in a mortar. (Rasārṇava 11.116)
Then, having placed it in a mechanical press, heated with a steady fire day and night, one should extract it from the press while hot and grind it in a heated mortar. (Rasāyana 11.117)
Having kneaded the mass with mica and placed it therein, one should apply a *puṭa* (sealing).
Then it quickly falls into the womb [of the crucible] and one may easily digest it. (Rasārṇava 11.118)
Then, having placed it in a swinging apparatus (dolāyantra) together with a moist mass, on the third day the mercury digests and subsequently swallows [the substance]. (Rasārṇava 11.119)
Then, O Pārvatī, until it is thoroughly digested, the wise one should process it in a swinging apparatus (dolāyantra);
thereafter, once it is thoroughly digested, he should digest it with a tortoise apparatus (kacchapayantra) using a dose equal to one-twelfth of the mass. (Rasārṇava 11.120)
As before, one should apply the *ārdraka* (ginger) preparation and the process of melting the interior (*garbhadrāvaṇa*);
thereafter, O Goddess, having placed that [substance] inside, the wise practitioner should provide the *puṭa* (sealing). Ras_11.121 //

Then, with one-eighth part [of the mercury], one should perform the swallowing (*grāsa*) and the melting of the embryo (*garbhadrāva*) as before; having cast that *sūtaka* (mercury) into the interior of a *sūraṇa* bulb, one should seal it in a *puṭa* until the bulb is no longer consumed by fire. (Rasārṇava 11.122)
A dose for the crucible is prescribed as one-fourth part of the mercury;
and as before, one should apply the *viḍa* salt and indeed the process of melting the embryo (*garbhadrāvaṇa*). (Rasārṇava 11.123)
When the fourfold [additives] have thus been digested, the mercury (sūtaka) becomes powerful;
thereafter, the mercury situated in the fire consumes the morsels with the probe (śalākā). (Rasārṇava 11.124)
Then, however, the noble gems [are to be purified] according to the sequence that will be described. (Rasāyana 11.125)
Having added mica, magnetite, and likewise conch-shell navel, together with the primary and secondary juices combined with the great digestives (mahājāraṇa), [one should proceed]. (Rasārṇava 11.126)
One should cook *vajrakanda*, *vajralatā*, *meṣaśṛṅgī*, *amṛtā*, iron, the seeds of *kaṭutumbī*, and dead metals. (Rasārṇava 11.127)
All [the ingredients] should be in equal proportions and moistened with peacock blood; the wise one should grind them until the medicinal preparation becomes firm. (Rasāyana 11.128)
A crucible (mūṣā) in the shape of a cow's ear (vallākṛti) should be prepared along with its covers;
one should place the mercury (sūta) in its middle and heat it with a downward-blowing bellows. (Rasārṇava 11.129)
At the outset, one should apply a vajra smeared with medicinal herbs to that very spot;
who would have any doubt about this being grasped, just as in the case of a fierce fire? (Rasāyana 11.130)
When the crucible has been burnt by the *kuliśa* [mineral], one should grind it with that [substance] in the fire of a pit;
thus, one should cause the *kuliśa* to digest [the mercury] until it has become eleven times its original weight. (Ras_11.131)
Pearl should then be added, together with well-burnt conch-shell navel soaked in the juice of *mātuluṅga*, once the mercury has been fully digested by the diamond. (Rasārṇava 11.132)
By this sequential method, it indeed becomes elevenfold;
likewise, pure peacock bile mixed with indigo extract [attains the same]. (Rasāyana 11.133)

Blue lotuses that have been smeared and cast into the *sūtaka* [mercury] should, according to the procedure for the elixir, abandon those of inferior color and take up those of great luster. (Rasāyana 11.134)
One should smear [the vessel] with red substances, peacock bile, and the great jewel; by means of that excellent jewel, it will flow out from the midst of the mercury. (Rasāyana 11.135)
Having impregnated *rajanī* and *kuṣṭha* with the exudate of *brahmī*, one should administer that very mixture for the digestion (*jāraṇa*) of the *puṣparāga*. (Rasārṇava 11.136)

O Goddess of good vows, when many jewels have been worn away and the *bhṛṅgarāga* has faded, the lord of mercury (*rasendra*) is seen, O Goddess, possessing a blue, yellow, and reddish luster. (Rasārṇava 11.137)
One should smear pure gold leaves with [the powder] in a hundredth part [of their weight] and kill them by means of a *puṭa* [firing]; it will become like an *indragopa* insect. (Ras 11.138)
O beloved, by mere contact, all this dead gold is pierced; one should then refine it together with a third part of the king of elixirs (sūtaka). (Rasārṇava 11.139)

O Goddess, when that [mercury] is situated within the crucible, one should again cause it to digest by means of that very [substance]; having been processed and digested, it becomes a penetrator by fumes (dhūmavedhī). Ras_11.140.
If, by this sequential method, the triple chain is digested, it will pierce the mountains, the netherworld, and the surface of the earth; of this there is no doubt. (Rasārṇava 11.141)
If the light is visible on the sides but not at all above, one should know that to be the earth-walker (bhūcara) mercury; of this there is no doubt. (Ras 11.142)
By that means, O Goddess, one of unceasing gait shall travel a hundred yojanas;
possessing divine splendor, a great body, divine vision, and immense strength. (Ras 11.143)
Freed from all diseases, he shall live as long as the moon and stars;
even his urine and feces will dissolve all metals. (Rasārṇava 11.144)
When thoroughly digested by means of vajra together with gold, and situated within fire, it dissolves the metals; thus the mercury (sūtaka) attains a stable bond. (Rasārṇava 11.145)
One should cause that [mercury] to digest with that seed and then pierce it a thousand times;
thereafter, one should cause the digested [substance] to digest, and it should be smeared upon and cast [into the crucible] thousands of times.
One should cause [the mercury] to flow by means of that seed; thereby one attains penetration of a hundred thousand (*lakṣavedha*).
By this sequential yoga, the mercury becomes capable of penetration of ten million (*koṭivedhī*). (Rasāyana 11.147)
But when one causes the vajra alone to be completely digested, then the mercury is known to be bound—unshakable and free from affliction. (Rasāyana 11.148)
The *sūta* (mercury), situated in fire, is born; in an instant it swallows the *śalākā* (the rod).
Being smelted by the forceful fire (*haṭhāgni*), it eagerly swallows everything. (Rasārṇava 11.149)
The mercury moves and ages, yet it bestows longevity and wealth;
one should blow upon the mercury situated in the crucible with a fierce fire, and it does not tremble at all. (Rasārṇava 11.150)
One should digest all the gems; when bound, it leads to the state of a sky-walker (khecaratā).
Thus, when the metal has been digested eight times over, there shall be the binding of the mercury. (Rasāyana 11.151)
Metals, the [inner] being, the three qualities, and likewise gold with its two qualities;
when it pierces through the vision of smoke, the mercury becomes the giver of nirvāṇa.
First, one should digest the great essence (mahārasa), the sattva of the sky, which possesses eight qualities;
then, one should digest diamonds and gems along with an equal amount [of the base metal] and one-tenth part of gold. Ras_11.153.
When one has digested all [the impurities], that mercury becomes a "sky-walker" (khecara) vajra;
it revolves in a clockwise direction and becomes capable of piercing ten million [parts]. (Rasāyana 11.154)
When the snake-skin is equal [in weight] to the mercury, the mercury becomes a hundred-fold piercer (daśavedhī);
when it is double, it becomes a hundred-fold piercer; and when it is triple, it becomes a thousand-fold piercer. (Rasārṇava 11.155)
O Goddess, one should increase it fourfold by this sequence;
through this progressive increase, one should digest the mercury therein. (Rasārṇava 11.156)

O Goddess of the gods, by heating that crooked, aged snake [mercury] according to the sequence of numbers, it attains that state of discourse; the mercury becomes a "koṭivedhī" (one that penetrates ten million times). Ras_11.157.
O Goddess of the gods, the sharp [mercury] that has been processed twelve times is consumed by the lord of the Dānavas, Ruru, as a calcinated ash-essence (bhasmasūtaka). (Rasārṇava 11.158)
Having consumed one *pala* [of it], the Dānava, arrogant in his strength, uprooted the world and even pulverized Kailāsa. (Ras 11.159)
There, having reflected for a moment and having seen that which was produced by his illusion,
[he saw] the molten lead and mercury, struck with an equal portion of mica, within the serpent.
O daughter of the snowy mountain, with that trident smeared by that marrow, the Dānava, arrogant in his strength, was slain by that spear. (Ras 11.161)
One should digest gold, copper, as well as *tīkṣṇa*, *vājara*, *ṣaḍālaka*, *rohaṇa*, and *kāntaloha* according to the number of the *tattvas*. (Rasārṇava 11.162)

Each of these individual kings of mercury, when bound, leads to the state of moving through the sky; O Goddess, listen now to how digestion becomes easy once the sulphur-lead (gandhanāga) has been liquefied. (Rasārṇava 11.163)
First, mercury that has been purified should be combined with the powder of *rajanī* (turmeric) and rubbed until it turns black; then it should be washed with warm *kāñjika*. (Rasāyana 11.164)
Thus, when rubbed again and again, the scent-elephant (gandhanāga) will undergo liquefaction.
O Goddess of the Gods, having repeatedly stirred the urine of a serpent, or that of a calf or a buffalo, one should sprinkle the serpent seven times. (Rasārṇava 11.166)
O beautiful one, having made its leaves capable of being pierced by thorns, one should add sulphur in a proportion equal to one-fourth [of the leaf's weight]. (Rasārṇava 11.167)
Having spread a layer of lac, followed by hair, then a powder of sulfur above that, and likewise a leaf of *nāgadalā*. (Rasārṇava 11.168)
Having spread out sulphur, human hair, and a layer of lac in succession, and having placed them upright, one should fashion a wick using threads. (Rasārṇava 11.169)
One should place it in the midst of karañja oil for ten nights;
then, having cut that wick, whose tip is glowing, one should hold it in pieces. (Rasaratnasamuccaya 11.170)
One should cause that liquid to fall into a vessel containing Sauvīra and Ṭaṅkaṇa;
O Dear One, one should then place that oil inside a glass flask. (Rasārṇava 11.171)

O Goddess, having placed the mercury in a plastered crucible shaped like a cow’s udder, one should determine its strength or weakness by means of the sixty-fourth part and so forth. (Rasārṇava 11.172)

O Goddess worshipped by the gods, having added the *gandhanāga* flux to that crucible and placed it in a pit filled with cow dung, one should apply the *puṭapācana* (sealed-furnace heating) using two handfuls (*prasṛti*) of dried cow-dung and husks. (Rasārṇava 11.173)
One should administer four drops of the juice of *siṃhavallī* into the mouth in case of suspected indigestion, as previously described; thus it should be done every day. (Rasāyana 11.174)
Through threefold digestion (jāraṇā), the mercury becomes the color of the jambū fruit. (Rasārṇava 11.175)
Taking a very small amount of *mākṣika* essence combined with dead lead (*nāga*), one should place it in a crucible;
after adding glass (*kāca*) both below and above, it should be well-heated in this manner twelve times until it becomes colored. (Rasārṇava 11.176)
The roasted powder of the seed, weighing one-quarter part, should be ground with sour chickpea juice in mercury; in an instant, internal liquefaction (garbhadruti) occurs. (Rasārṇava 11.177)

O Goddess, if there is no internal liquefaction (*garbhadruti*) of the two colors and the fragrance, then the seed, smeared with a paste made from red mineral (*raktasindūra*), *sindhūdbhava* (rock salt), *alarka*, *ṭaṅkaṇa* (borax), and *āśugapuṅkha* (saltpeter), and subjected to the *puṭa* process, will become liquefied within. (Rasārṇava 11.178)

When the seed has been digested for a portion equal to half a quarter (one-eighth) [of the total], it performs the *vedha* (penetration) by means of the tenth, sixteenth, and twenty-second parts respectively. (Rasārṇava 11.179)

Having combined the three-fold alloy with silver, and having smeared this "silver-poison" (tārāriṣṭa) with the remaining silver, one should perform the transmutation (vedha) using that mercury. (Ras 11.180)

Henceforth, O Goddess, I shall describe the refinement [of mercury] through the digestion (*jāraṇa*) of *nāga* and *abhra*: having powdered red oleander (*karavīrāruṇā*) and realgar (*manaḥśilā*), [one should apply it]. (Rasārṇava 11.181)
One should infuse [the substance] twenty times with the juice of *yavaciñcā*.
Having carefully smeared a *nāga* leaf with that paste, one should cook it over a charcoal fire until it becomes powdered. (Ras 11.182)
One should grind three parts of mercury, one part of cinnabar, and a quarter-part each of sulphur, mica, and poison with citron juice. (Rasārṇava 11.183)

When that lead has been subjected to *puṭapāka* (closed-vessel heating) in a crucible smeared with this paste, one should blow it [into the furnace] in this manner seven times, and it will become like gold. (Rasārṇava 11.184)
Yellow mica with a single leaflet, smeared with black pepper inside a crucible, should be heated until it glows like fire and then cast into the juice of *saubhāñjana*. (Rasārṇava 11.185)
One should cause that being, radiant with gold, to fall according to the previously described procedure.
The leaf of tin (nāga) and the essence of yellow mica (pītābhra),
combined with these— cow's milk, glass-smoke, guñjā, magnetite, ṭaṅkaṇa,
and combined with tuttha— this becomes the "tin-mica" (nāgābhra) compound. (Rasārṇava 11.187)

Alternatively, one should grind mercury for three days with *kiṃvāra*, *nāla*, *siddhārtha*, *dhūmasāra*, brick, and molasses, and then subject it to heating in a *dolāyantra* for three days. (Rasārṇava 11.188)

Then, one should again subject it to heating in a *dolāyantra* for three days, combined with a paste of *punarnavā*, *meṣaśṛṅgī*, and *sarpākṣī*, along with *athāsurī*, *sindhu* salt, and poison (*viṣa*), all finely ground with black pepper (*marica*). (Rasārṇava 11.189)
O Goddess of the Gods, having administered *nāgābhra* at one-eighth part [of the dose], there should be two parts of *śilā* and one part of *sindhusauvarcala*. (Rasārṇava 11.190)

Half a ṭaṅka of mercury and a quarter-part of poison, along with one-eighth of a bolus of viḍa salt, should be digested over three days in the "tortoise" [vessel]; in this manner, it should be digested six times over. (Rasārṇava 11.191)
Stone, tuttha, uraga, copper, tīkṣṇaloha, ghoṣa, arka, and gold—these increase in sequence through the precipitation of the essence of tāpya. (Rasārṇava 11.192)
One should cause that seed, remaining as dross, to be processed with a quarter-part of mātulā water; one should digest it with the king of fluids (mercury) along with gold. (Rasārṇava 11.193)

O Goddess of the Gods, having placed [the mercury] in a lotus-apparatus (*padmayantra*) with *tāpya*, *sauvarcala*, *śilā*, sulphur, *kāsīsa*, and *ṭaṅkaṇa*, and then having inserted a peg, [one should proceed]. (Rasārṇava 11.194)
One should gently heat it for three days until the seed becomes liquefied; that very rasa, when fully digested and motionless within the fire, [is ready]. (Rasāyana 11.195)

Then, by means of the seed-mantra of the six qualities (ṣaḍguṇabīja) through the sequential application of the process of amalgamation (sāraṇā), one should transmute lead, silver, and copper with a thousandth part [of the elixir]. (Rasāyana 11.196)
With a paste of viṣagandha, tāpya, abhraka, crow-dung, ghanadhvani, sahadevī, and vahniśikhā, the mercury is transmuted. (Rasārṇava 11.197)
The fainted mercury, the dead mercury, and the leech-binding;
the fourth is the form-binding, while the fifth is the bandage-binding;
the ash-mercury and the solidified globule (khoṭa)—thus mercury is sevenfold through its purification processes. (Rasārṇava 11.198)
That mercury which has abandoned its dense volatility and possesses the color of a serpent, and whose characteristic signs are visible, is indeed said to be "fainted" (mūrchita). (Rasārṇava 11.199)
One should know that [mercury] in which moisture, density, brilliance, heaviness, and volatility are not observed is dead lead. (Rasārṇava 11.200)
Multicolored and likewise clear, the *sūtaka* is bound within the womb like a leech, possessing the characteristic of being attached like a leech. (Rasārṇava 11.201)
Heaviness and redness, resembling the brilliance of the sun, should remain held within the center of the flame; this is the characteristic of the binding of the form (mūrtibandha).
Or else, through the process of incineration with a rod (śalākājāraṇā), the state of being bound in form (mūrtibandha) is desired.
When it is white, yellow, heavy, soft, and resembles beeswax, and remains in the midst of fire, that is the characteristic of *paṭṭabandha*. (Rasārṇava 11.204)

When blackness, whiteness, yellowness, blueness, and ash-likeness have disappeared, that is the characteristic of the "ash-mercury" (bhasmasūta) when its volatility has been destroyed. (Rasārṇava 11.205)
When the mercury is like a hen’s egg and breaks through salt, the liquid thus revolves; such is the characteristic of the *khoṭaka* state. (Rasārṇava 11.206)
Alternatively, when being cut, it should be unctuous; it should melt with a soft ray [of light].
The characteristic of the *khoṭabandha* is that it is indestructible, hard, and white. (Rasārṇava 11.207)

As for the five substances beginning with *khoṭa*, once they have been cast into the shape of leeches and smelted in the fire of *haṭha*, they do not remain at all, having become liquefied (*mūrchita*). (Rasārṇava 11.208)
Resembling the rising sun and possessing various colors, O Goddess of the Gods, the colored Rasabhairava pierces the metals of the body. (Rasārṇava 11.209)

First comes the purification of the mercury (sūtaka), then the measurement of the morsel (grāsa), followed by the digestion (jāraṇa) of the essence of the sky (vyomasattva) and the digestion of all essences. (Rasārṇava 11.210)
Next is the liquefaction of the interior and exterior [of the mercury], followed by the digestion (*jāraṇa*) of gold;
then the application of divine medicinal herbs (*divyauṣadhi*), and after that, the binding with jewels (*ratnabandha*). (Rasārṇava 11.211)
And after that, O Goddess, coloring (rañjana), digestion (jāraṇā), and subsequent processing (anusāraṇā) should be performed;
then penetration (krāmaṇa) should be administered to the mercury (sūtaka) by the wise. (Rasārṇava 11.212)
For one who knows this sequence in this way, there is accomplishment without a doubt. (Ras 11.213)
He who knows the piercing [process] (*vedhaka*) in relation to the body, metals, and alchemy (*rasāyana*), his birth, old age, and disease are destroyed; of this there is no doubt. (Rasāyana 11.214)
Within the body, however, there are five jewels: nāga, vaṅga, iron, mercury, and the king of fluids (rasarāja); these are the medicine that causes penetration and destroys disease. (Rasārṇava 11.215)
Through the sequence of the power of its application, mercury proceeds by means of medicinal herbs;
it advances against the multitude of diseases and devours malignant illness. (Rasārṇava 11.216)
Having understood its transmutation (*krāmaṇa*), one should then treat it with medicinal preparations.
Without transmutation, mercury does not undergo transference nor does it effect penetration;
[consequently,] all ailments of the body and metals would remain, and the effort alone would be in vain. (Rasārṇava 11.217)
Whichever formulation is appropriate for whichever disease, one should administer it with that very same [remedy];
thus the king of mercury (rasendra) removes the ailments of men, elephants, and horses. (Ras 11.218)
In its raw state (āroṭa), mercury bestows strength; when swooned (mūrchita), it destroys disease;
when bound (baddha), it grants the perfection of Khecarī; and when killed (mārita), it brings about freedom from old age and death. (Rasārṇava 11.219)
Mercury, when specifically pacified by disease, combined with sulphur, and killed by medicinal herbs, does not live again. (Rasārṇava 11.220)
"O Mistress of the Gods, tell me that which penetrates the metals; by means of that one should prepare an elixir (*rasāyana*). What else do you wish to hear?
The Goddess said:
O Lord, what kind of auspicious medicinal herb causes the intensification of the mercury?
By what means does the mercury become ash-like, and by what means is the solidification (khoṭa-bandhana) achieved? (Rasārṇava 12.1)

The illustrious Bhairava said: Listen attentively, O Bhairavī, honored by heroes, to this secret of binding mercury, which is not known even by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Indra, and the other gods. (Rasārṇava 12.2)
Between the Gaṅgā and Yamunā, there is a Rākṣasa named Prayoga;
O lady of excellent hips, in his vicinity, a newborn child would be bound in an instant. (Ras 12.3)
The best of practitioners should take the leaves of the night-walker (niśācara);
O Goddess, when pressed below, it becomes the most excellent juice. (Ras 12.4)
Having ground the mercury with that very [substance] for three days, the alchemist should quickly fix the *āroṭa* and digest the *gagana* (mica) therein. (Rasārṇava 12.5)
Furthermore, one should prepare the *gagana* (mercury) with that very leaf-juice;

having been processed seven times with that [juice] together with the three pungents (*tryūṣaṇa*), O Goddess, one should cause the *gagana* to be digested there in the *vidyādhara* apparatus. (Rasārṇava 12.6)
Within just one month, O Goddess of gods, that [mercury] is digested equally;
when the mercury is fully digested, O Goddess, it becomes a hundred-fold penetrator (śatavedhī).
Then, O Goddess, one should saturate the sulphur with the juice of *niśācara*, and then saturate it seven times with the juice of *dvipadī*. (Rasārṇava 12.8)
By applying a leaf-coating of silver, [the mercury] becomes excellent gold of half-and-half [purity];
when this has been fully digested in sulphur, the mercury becomes a hundred-fold penetrator (śatavedhī).
Having added that sulphur again for a leaf-coating, one should remove the *ravi* [copper];
then, one should process that *ravi* three times within the silver (*tāra*). (Rasārṇava 12.10)
Gold mixed with half its weight of mercury attains equality with the Mātṛkā;
then, having directly melted that sulphur, make it flow rapidly. (Rasārṇava 12.11)
One should grind the king of mercury (rasendra) with that [substance] and cause it to penetrate the body;
by merely applying an ointment of that very [mixture], O Dear One, it destroys the eighteen types of leprosy, hemorrhoids, fistula-in-ano, spider-bites, and diseases of the head. (Ras 12.12)
One should saturate the mineral calamine (tālaka) seven times with the juice of *niśācara* (night-walker);
with that very [juice], one should strike tin (*vaṅga*), and the tin should be dissolved into silver (*tāra*). (Rasārṇava 12.13)
One should dissolve that silver (tāra) in mercury; that mercury then undergoes fixation.
By merely anointing [the metal] with that alone, it becomes sixty-four times [its original weight]. (Rasārṇava 12.14)
One should cause the application of copper-penetration (śulvavedha) at the sixty-fourth part;
one should apply that copper to silver, and that silver shall become gold.
That gold becomes most excellent, bestowing virtue, pleasure, wealth, and liberation. (Rasārṇava 12.15)

One should have the flowers of the night-stalker (niśācara) made into a fine powder; ten palas of this powder should then be saturated with the juices of the emblic myrobalan (dhātrī). (Rasakalpa 12.16)
Having mixed it with ghee and honey, one should place it in a new vessel;
O Goddess of the Gods, it should be buried in a heap of grain for twenty-one days. (Rasāyana 12.17)
By merely consuming that, one becomes free from wrinkles and grey hair.
One should lick the fine powder of *valkala* mixed with honey;
by its use for half a month, O beloved, this [elixir] shall become manifest. (Rasāyana 12.19)
By means of its urine and feces, copper becomes gold;
by application for just one month, even a serpent becomes gold.
One should collect that oil from the fruit in the apparatus known as *pātāla*;
with that oil, O Goddess of Gods, the wise one should cause the mercury to contract. (Rasārṇava 12.21)
At that very moment, O Goddess, the great elixir becomes bound with a turban.
O fair-faced one, a pungent bracelet should be fashioned upon the mercury-linga;
by means of that, the most wonderful act of contraction and slaying should be performed. (Ras 12.23)
The sun [substance] should be cast seven times into the juice of *niśācara* (night-stalker); freed from blackness by that process, it becomes radiant like gold. (Rasārṇava 12.24)

The external [substance] should be sprinkled and sown together with that *tārā* (silver); one should then subject the mercury (*sūta*) to *vedha* in a ratio of one part [of the external substance] to ten parts [of mercury], and when it has been drunk [assimilated], it should be subjected to *vedha* again in a ratio of one part to a hundred. Ras_12.25 //
It pierces a hundred, a target, a thousand, and ten million;
it may pierce ten million with a tenth part, and likewise by means of that which pierces ten million. (Rasāyana 12.26)
I shall further proclaim another [method], the binding of mercury, which is very difficult to obtain. Ras_12.27 //
That herb which is the mother of the three worlds and the mistress of the unborn—by the mere contact with it, mercury becomes bound. (Rasāyana 12.28)
Having been macerated for seven days with the juice of that great medicinal herb, it produces divine gold through a transmutation by even a hundredth part [of its weight]. (Rasārṇava 12.29)

O lady of excellent complexion, by rubbing the mercury with that [substance] for two weeks, the mercury becomes a direct piercer of one hundred thousand [parts], turning the eight metals into gold. (Rasārṇava 12.30)
O Goddess of the gods, within three weeks it pierces ten lakhs;
and in the fourth week, the great mercury becomes a crore-piercer. (Rasārṇava 12.31)
When rubbed with the juice of the great medicinal herb after being heated and sweated, it bestows the siddhi of moving through the sky, its range becoming unimpeded. (Rasāyana 12.32)
One may enjoy a thousand amorous women within a single day;
indeed, with one's shadow vanished and oneself invisible, one shall wander through the three worlds with [alchemical] essences. (Ras 12.33)
By the very juice of the great medicinal herb (mahauṣadhī), the restoration of the dead occurs;
by this, O beloved, one should kill the mercury and bring it to the five stages.
One should cause nasal drops to be administered to the deceased and massage his hands and feet;
O fair-faced one, the life-force of even the dead shall then enter him. (Rasārṇava 12.35)
I shall now further explain the binding of mercury, which is very difficult to attain:
by means of the essence of human flesh alone, mercury is bound in an instant. (Rasārṇava 12.36)
Having added the essence of *narasāra* together with the dust of *dvipadī*, it forms a bond at the end of the day; one should thus color all metals. (Rasārṇava 12.37)

O Goddess, once the mercury has been digested by the essence of *narasāra* six times over, one should impregnate that mercury with realgar (*manaḥśilā*), whether it be in silver or copper. (Rasārṇava 12.38)
If that [plant] grows without fragrance, it destroys the elixir;
however, by means of the dust of *dvipadī* together with it, one becomes a serpent devoid of life-force. (Rasāyana 12.39)
O Goddess, when the mercury has been digested by the essence of *narasāra* six times over,
it becomes capable of piercing even silver or copper to the depth of ten million units.

Having performed seven separate saturations of the mercury with the essence of *narasāra* in milk, one should cause the mercury to swallow a morsel (*grāsa*) in the apparatus called *vidyādhara*. (Rasārṇava 12.41)
O Goddess, O lady of beautiful countenance, the mouthless *gagana* is digested by the essence of *narasāra* and the juice of *kīṭamārī*.
O Goddess, it dissolves *gagana*, as well as *tīkṣṇa* iron and *pannaga*. (Rasāyana 12.42)
O beloved of the Sun, through the juice of *narasāra* and the juice of *hanūmatī*, divine gold is produced by means of *niṣeka*. (Rasārṇava 12.43)

Having added mañjiṣṭhā and red sandalwood to the essence of narasāra, one should then grind it in its own juice; O Goddess, one should subsequently sprinkle the snake [preparation] with this. (Rasāyana 12.44)
O Goddess, at that very moment, that divine gold, having been infused seven times and rubbed by the sun, becomes threefold in weight, O beloved, like a serpent. (Rasārṇava 12.45)
That mercury, resembling gold and joined with five parts of silver, combined with one-eighth part of gold, is the medicinal agent for the work of gold-making. (Rasārṇava 12.46)
Cinnabar should be processed seven times with the juice of *narasāra* (the essence of man);
with that very [juice], one should reduce the sharp metal (*tīkṣṇa*) to ashes, which is designated as the state of being reduced to ash. (Rasārṇava 12.47)
That ash, ground with copper, should be combined with three times that amount of the latter.

That mercury (śulva) resembles gold; when combined with one-eighth part of silver (tāra), it becomes silver-gold (tārahema). When equal parts of silver and gold are used, the resulting brass (pittala) shall be double [the amount]. (Ras_12.49)
One should saturate the *rasaka* seven times with the essence of human marrow;
then that *rasa*, the *rasaka*, *tīkṣṇa* iron, and *pannaga* [mercury]— [are to be combined]. (Rasārṇava 12.50)
One should grind that very essence of the best of men together with that [mercury] in one place;
at that moment, the binding of both the mercury and the mercurial product occurs.
One should likewise color sharp nāga and copper with *rasaka*;
the resulting whole becomes gold with the luster of a *kūṣmāṇḍa* flower. (Ras_12.51)
I shall further proclaim another [method], the binding of mercury, which is very difficult to obtain.
O Supreme Goddess, there is a medicinal herb named Kaṅkālakhecarī;
having collected its oil and combining it with Māghakhecarī,
one should infuse it for one day in a vessel made of solar metal (gold).
When the second day arrives, one should strike the diamond-gem (vajraratna) and heat it in fire until it possesses the radiance of intensely glowing flames. (Rasārṇava 12.54)
One should soak a diamond-gem in the oil of the Kaṅkālakhecarī plant ten times; once soaked thus, it indeed turns into the form of ash. (Rasāyana 12.55)
One should reduce that gold-ripened seed to ashes with that [reagent];
having added one-third part of borax (*ṭaṅkaṇa*), one should blow it in a blind crucible (*andhamūṣā*).
At that very moment, the pair—the diamond-gem and the gold—will merge together. (Rasārṇava 12.56)

O lady of excellent hips, if mercury is processed with equal parts of silver and gold, O Goddess, it becomes a "ten-million-penetration" (*koṭivedhī*) elixir and pierces the eight metals. (Rasārṇava 12.57)
I shall now further proclaim the binding of mercury, which is extremely difficult to attain.
O Beloved, one should take medicinal herbs that possess seeds, as well as certain shrubs and creepers;
O Goddess, the second is named Mantrasiṃhāsanī, which is Khecarī.
One should collect that oil from the Pātālayantra into a copper vessel. (Rasārṇava 12.59)
Into the midst of that oil, one should pour the essence of *khecarī*;
then, O fair-faced one, one should place it within the *medinī* apparatus. (Rasārṇava 12.60)
O Goddess, by means of that aforementioned herb, [place] the sky upon the surface of the earth;
then, having given the mercury its "swallow" (rasagrāsa), form a ball (golaka) through grinding. (Rasārṇava 12.61)
Having bound it into a pill with that [substance], one should cause the mercury to digest within the sky;
when the sky has been digested evenly, the bound mercury remains stable. (Rasārṇava 12.62)
When it is blown with the force of bellows, its form perishes; once fully digested, it becomes like crow-dung. (Rasāyana 12.63)
When the sky has doubled and aged, one should collect the eight metals.
Furthermore, I shall proclaim another [method], the binding of mercury, which is very difficult to obtain.
The herb Turasiṃhanī, produced from the body of Śiva, dissolves sulphur; it likewise dissolves orpiment. (Rasārṇava 12.66)
It shall digest gold, and it shall bind the lord of mercury;
it shall digest coral and likewise liquefy the sky (aerial minerals);
it shall destroy the diamond and cause all living beings to fall [under its power]. (Rasārṇava 12.67)
One should digest all metals and even cause the *sattvas* to cook;
having placed [the substance] in the juice of *harīndarī*, O fair-faced one, it should be deposited within a cow's horn.
It should then be buried in a heap of grain; thus the mercury remains in a state of death. (Rasāyana 12.68)

O Goddess worshipped by the gods, when the mercury has been digested in an equal amount of gold with the juice of a divine herb, it will then penetrate ten koṭis [of times its weight]. (Rasārṇava 12.69)
In the fifth [stage], one pierces a hundred million *lakṣas*; in the sixth, one pierces by touch;
in the seventh, one becomes a piercer of smoke; in the eighth, however, by sight;
in the ninth, one becomes a piercer of sound; beyond this, it does not exist.
Foolish beings wander like cattle, deprived of the medicinal plants of the [spiritual] lineage; for no accomplishment whatsoever arises from the juices of ordinary grass and herbs. (Rasāyana 12.71)
Therefore, with every effort, the Kula-herb must indeed be known. (Rasārṇava 12.72)
The sixty-four divine medicinal herbs are established within the Kula;
yet those fools, deluded by divine illusion, do not know them at all.
Non-divine grasses and medicinal herbs grow in mountain caves.
Mercury is never bound by the juice of grass-herbs;
O beautiful lady, it remains inexhaustible and does not stay within the midst of fire. (Rasāyana 12.75)
It is neither dross nor ash, nor does it produce any substance; what substance could it possibly produce? Being smelted, it does not remain [as such]. (Rasāyana 12.76)
O beloved, that mercury does not remain in gold during heating, melting, cutting, or piercing; nor does it undergo piercing beyond one hundred [times]. Ras 12.77.
O beloved, as long as even a single piece has not been bound and sold as gold,
one should never give it away for the sake of dharma, artha, kāma, or mokṣa.
The Goddess said:
"O Śaṅkara, the charioteer has become lifeless; how can he give life? How can that which is lifeless cause that which is lifeless to live? (Ras 12.79)
The illustrious Bhairava said:
O Goddess, when the mercury (rasendra) has been rendered inert by a divine herb, yet is devoid of Kālikā, then, O Pārvatī, that mercury becomes [unstable]. (Rasārṇava 12.80)
The mercury free from blackness robs the time of another;
it pacifies the impurities of the eight metals in an instant. (Rasāyana 12.81)
Whoever might say that a charioteer who has fallen into a great swoon is dead, that one whose consciousness is lost is restored to life by the very essence of a divine herb. (Rasārṇava 12.82)
The mercury, whose essence consists of the five elements, remains as Sadāśiva himself.
O Īśvarī, I shall further explain the binding of mercury.
One should bind together in one place the vajra killed by the protector of the earth (kṣmāpāla) and the gold killed by that very same [substance]—that is, vajra-ash and gold-ash. (Rasārṇava 12.85)
Having processed [the mercury] in the juice of *niśācara*, one should digest it with human semen;
O auspicious lady, one should then kill that mercury using the divine medicinal herbs *gajāri* and *divyaka*.
He who has consumed that mercury is Sadāśiva himself in person;
by consuming even a single *tolaka* of it, a man becomes capable of the alchemical transmutation through touch (*sparśavedhī*). (Rasārṇava 12.87)
From the perspiration of that body, the king of essences (mercury) is extracted;
and from the perspiration as well as the urine, the eight metals and gold [are obtained].
That supreme practitioner shall live for a hundred thousand years;
possessing the dark splendor of Prajāpati, he binds the impurity (sūtaka) in an instant. (Rasārṇava 12.89)
O Goddess, one is bound by the king through the touch of an elephant or a lion. (Rasārṇava 12.90)
O beloved, when the mercury (gagana) is processed with the juice of *vajravallī* and subjected to distillation in a *vālukāyantra*, it becomes a solid *khoṭa* in that very instant. (Rasāyana 12.91)

Having combined one *māṣa* of dead lead globule (*mṛtagolaka*) and one *māṣa* of gold globule, and having thoroughly ground them together with lime juice (*luṅgāmla*) for three days, one should smear the leaves of the *nāga* plant with one *karṣa* of this liquid paste. (Rasārṇava 12.92)
One should wrap it with *vṛścikālī* and then smear that bolus;
thus, O Goddess, one kills the serpent, which becomes like a *śakragopa* insect. (Rasārṇava 12.93)
One should smear one *karṣa* of silver leaves with dead lead (*nāga*) and with *vṛścikālī*;
then, once those leaves have been smeared, they should be wrapped up. (Rasārṇava 12.94)
O Goddess, that silver which resembles the redness of vermilion dies away;
by means of that very [substance] in its thousandth part, one should cause the piercing of the copper to be performed. (Rasārṇava 12.95)
Divine gold is produced, serving as an ornament for the jewelry of the gods.
O Pārvatī, that which is milky, possesses many fruits, and has joints is praised by the name Caṭulaparṇī for the binding of mercury. (Rasārṇava 12.97)
In the *ekavīrākandara* crucible, one should blow upon the mercury contained in a sealed crucible using the breath from the mouth; thus bound, it is recommended for consumption. (Rasārṇava 12.98)
The bulb of the red-robe plant (raktakañcukī), ground with breast milk and placed in a crucible according to the previous method, effects the binding of mercury. (Rasārṇava 12.99)
One should heat the seed of *vṛścikāpattrikā* combined with women’s milk as before; thus the alchemist obtains mercury for the purpose of consumption. (Rasāyana 12.100)
Taking *vajrakanda*, one should cast it into the midst of the mercury;
having applied the *puṭa* known as "Lord of Elephants" (*gajendra*), one should bring it to a state of being bound seven times. (Ras 12.101)
The wise one should consume that elixir; within six months, he shall become immortal.
Having taken the tuber of *lāṅgalī* and the tuber of *karkoṭī*, one should place the juice within them, then subject it to steaming and grind it again. (Rasārṇava 12.103)
It dies here, there is no doubt, when blown with a fierce fire;
one should then seal and heat the mercury that has entered the parrot’s beak. (Rasāyana 12.104)
This piercer shall produce bodily perfection even from a hundredth part [of the substance]. (Rasārṇava 12.105)
One should place the juice of *haṃsapādī* and mercury inside the bulb of *śūkakaṇḍa*;
one should apply the "elephant-king" (*gajendra*) seal, and it dies—of this there is no doubt. (Rasāyana 12.106)
Having taken haṃsāṅghri and śukatuṇḍī, one should grind them with mercury; having placed this inside the belly of a krauñcapāda, one should then apply three *puṭa* roastings. (Rasārṇava 12.107)
The great elixir pierces the target; of this there is no doubt. (Rasāyana 12.108)
Listen, O beloved, to the description of the divine herb known as *tṛṇajyoti*.
It burns constantly at night, O Pārvatī, but it does not burn during the day.
If milk is poured at its root, O beloved, it turns into blood. (Rasārṇava 12.109)

A copper leaf smeared with mercury, sulphur, mica, and the juices and scents derived from those [ingredients], ground together with the sour juice of *mātuluṅga*, shall become gold after three *puṭa* roastings. (Rasārṇava 12.110)
O Goddess of the gods, the king of mercury combined with the powder of its root, when rubbed with the juice of *mātuluṅga*, causes mica to dissolve in an instant. (Rasārṇava 12.111)
Now, O beloved, I shall describe uccaṭī, which effects the binding of mercury;
it should consist of a single stalk, and its sheath should be made of hair. (Rasārṇava 12.112)
And at its tip there should be a flower resembling a parrot's beak;
its petals, O Queen of Gods, resemble the feathers of a parrot;
its bulb has the appearance of kuṣṭha, and its latex resembles vermilion. (Rasārṇava 12.113)
O Pārvatī, having taken beeswax that exudes from water, one should pierce all metals, and they become gold. (Rasārṇava 12.114)
One should grind mercury, orpiment, and blue vitriol with the juices of uccaṭī;
heated in the sun, the mercury dies through the power of the divine herb. (Rasārṇava 12.115)
O fair-faced one, one should pierce the seven metals with a one-in-a-lakṣa proportion.
Now, O beautiful goddess, I shall describe the ritual procedure for red snuhī:
one should apply a paste of leaf-juice made from the milky sap of snuhī onto copper. (Rasārṇava 12.117)
O fair-faced one, one should heat it again with milk seven times, until it becomes as radiant as Jāmbūnada gold. (Rasārṇava 12.118)
Then, one should cook it with sesame oil for three days;
likewise, when the leaves of copper are pierced [with this], they shall become gold.
One should pierce [the metal] with a thousandth part of the juice of red *snuhī*, its milky sap, realgar (*kunaṭī*), sulphur, mica (*abhraka*), cinnabar (*darada*), and the metals. (Rasārṇava 12.119)
Having taken the latex of *snuhī*, half a *niṣka* of gold, realgar, and fragrant powder, one should grind all of these together in one place. (Rasāyana 12.120)
In this very manner, one should purify gold for half a night;
having formed it into a pill, one pierces lead with that very [substance] at that instant. (Rasāyana 12.121)
Now, therefore, hear the procedure for the divine herb known as Sthalapadminī. Ras_12.122 //
It resembles a lotus in its leaves and likewise in its flowers;
upon breaking, it yields milk that is of a beautiful red color. (Rasāyana 12.123)
Having stepped upon it with her left foot, she should gaze at the circle of the sky;
she should behold the circle of planets and constellations joined with the stars.
O Goddess, that [place] should be known as the "Terrestrial Lotus" (sthalapadminī) from a distance of a hundred thousand yojanas. *Rasārṇava* 12.124.
Taking its five parts, combined with mercury and sulfur, along with realgar, orpiment, and honey. (Rasārṇava 12.125)
One should rub it for seven nights and then use it to transmute copper;
O Goddess of the Gods, when pierced by even a thousandth part of it, it becomes gold. (Rasārṇava 12.126)

O Dear One, having taken its five parts according to the previously mentioned procedure, one should cause the king of mercury to circulate and then blow it while it is contained within a mūka-mūṣā crucible. (Rasārṇava 12.127)
It dies among the mice due to contraction; of this there is no doubt.
With that very [substance], one should pierce all metals by a thousandth part. (Rasārṇava 12.128)
Now, therefore, O beloved, I shall fully explain the procedure for *kumudinī*;
having split a stone from Kashmir on the full moon day, one should perform [the rite]. (Ras 12.129)
Having taken its five parts, one should impregnate the realgar;
having placed it in a crucible, one should impregnate it again and again. (Rasārṇava 12.130)
Melt lead in an iron pan and mix it with that paste;
indeed, gold will certainly arise, equal in appearance to liquid saffron. (Rasārṇava 12.131)
I shall explain, in brief, that which is to be grasped from the *Citraka*. (Ras 12.132)
Citraka is known to be of three kinds: red, black, and white; for rejuvenation (rasāyana), the red is best, the black is middling, and the white is inferior.
For the alleviation of diseases, the white is best, the black is middling, and the red is the least effective. (Ras 12.133)
In the winter season, a wise person should not extract [the juice] that is black, red, or even white.
O Goddess, having uprooted black *citraka* that has not been smelled by cows, if it is placed in the midst of milk, the milk will turn black in an instant. (Rasārṇava 12.135)
One should grind mercury together with the powder of its five parts and blow it in a sealed crucible (*mūkamūṣā*); it becomes a solid bolus (*khoṭa*) at that very moment. (Rasāyana 12.136)
Having dressed in red garments and being adorned with red garlands and unguents,
O Great Goddess, on the fifth day of the dark fortnight, one should offer an oblation of red śāli rice and extract red citraka. (Ras 12.137)
By means of the powder of red *citraka*, [the metal] undergoes three heats each;
liberated from all defects, it attains fixity at that very moment. (Rasāyana 12.138)
Its root and *sūtaka* [mercury] should be placed in sour liquid (*amla*) and treated with *kaṅguṇī* oil;
after twenty-one applications, the copper (*śulva*) will become pure. (Rasārṇava 12.139)
O Goddess of Gods, when the leaf of *candrārka* is smeared with the oil of red *citraka* and *bhallātaka* and subjected to the *puṭa* process, it becomes beautiful gold. (Rasārṇava 12.140)
By applying a leaf-coating of *nāginīkanda*, *sūtendra* (mercury), and *raktacitraka*, the moon and sun (silver and copper) become gold. (Rasārṇava 12.141)
Even the juice combined with red citraka will be effective at all times.
I shall describe the procedure for Jyotiṣmatī oil; listen, O Pārvatī. (Rasārṇava 12.143)
There is a creeper named Jyotiṣmatī which resembles gold;
it is abundant with spreading vines and possesses auspicious fruits of golden hue. (Ras 12.144)
In the first fortnight of the month of Āṣāḍha, having taken the supreme seed and boiled it like sesame seeds using either the hands or the feet,
one should collect its oil and place it in a copper jar. (Rasāyana 12.145)
One should heat the vessel placed on the ground with a fire of husks, gradually increasing the intensity;
when six months have passed, that pot shall become gold.
Having prepared that [substance] made of gold and mixed with oil and honey, one should pour it during the process of counter-sprinkling; then that gold will become equal to copper. (Rasārṇava 12.147)
And thus, it shall pierce a hundred [targets], being the unsurpassed jewel of knowledge.
O beloved, I shall describe *dagdhārohā*, which effects the binding of mercury;
it should be known as effective for tactile transmutation (*sparśavedha*) and as the accomplisher of all purposes and goals. (Rasārṇava 12.149)
O Great Goddess, even when cut by a weapon or burnt by fire, this divine great medicinal herb grows back in an instant, though it has been burnt and severed. (Rasārṇava 12.150)
Its flower is produced as red, yellow, white, or black;
one should observe its well-developed leaves to resemble those of the chickpea plant. (Rasāyanatantra 12.151)
She is established on the bank of the Gomatī, at Gaṅgā, and on Mount Arbuda;
she is seen in the forest regions to the south of Ujjayinī.
A wise person should prepare a pill by combining its divine resin, which is marked with black streaks, with betel leaf. (Rasārṇava 12.153)
Having pierced a thousand units of all these molten metals within the midst of fire, one instantly produces gold. (Rasārṇava 12.154)
In the same way, the mercury, when combined with cinnabar, gold, and mica, undergoes death;
it produces divine gold, fit for the ornaments and jewelry of the gods.
O Goddess, hear now about the divine medicinal herb renowned as kaṭutumbī. (Ras 12.156)
Having collected its seeds, one should cause them to be made into a fine powder.
It should be processed twenty-one times with the juice of *dhātrī* (myrobalan) mixed with milk and combined with *viśvabheṣaja* (ginger). (Rasaka 12.158)
Having cast the seed into the apparatus and extracted the oil, the wise one should cause the mercury to swoon and then rub it with that *cakramarda*. (Rasārṇava 12.159)
Cow-bile and peacock-bile, combined with potassium carbonate (kāṅkṣī) and iron sulfate (kāsīsa), along with an equal amount of silver—all these are equal to mercury (sūtaka). (Rasārṇava 12.160)
It should be placed inside a ram's horn continuously for one month;
once saturated with an iron rod, it will pierce all metals. (Rasārṇava 12.161)
Sulfur processed twenty-one times with an iron rod, combined with this very iron and mixed with the juice of *jambīra* fruit; (Ras_12.162:1)
Having placed the seed-mercury together with the fluxing agent (*sūtaka*) inside a blind crucible (*andhamūṣā*),
and having buried it in the earth for one month, it shall transform silver into gold.
One part of *dala*, five parts of *tāra* (silver), five parts of *śulva* (copper), and one part of *bīja* should be combined. (Rasāyana 12.163)
These shall be twelve parts; one should place all of that upon the earth. One should perform the consecration (niṣeka) of this site by means of the "earth-staff" (bhūdaṇḍa). (Ras 12.164)
At the end of twenty-five days, however, the finest gold is produced.

I shall describe the procedure for the milk-tuber (*kṣīrakanda*), which is supreme and brings about all accomplishments; among the four types of tubers described therein, the red tuber is most highly praised. (Rasāyana 12.166)
When this is broken, milk of a beautiful red color flows forth. (Rasāyana 12.167)
Adorned with seven glossy petals resembling the *snuhī* plant, possessing the brilliant luster of gold and resonant with the roar of clouds,
this is the binding of the king of mercury (*rasarāja*), which brings all sentient beings under one's control. (Ras 12.168)
Having collected its milk, the wise one should quench the silver;
by blowing with a fire of *dhava* wood, beautiful gold is produced. (Rasārṇava 12.169)
A wise person should grind mercury with the sap of *tintiṇī* leaves mixed with a slight amount of copper dust; thus, the binding of the mercury will occur. (Rasārṇava 12.170)
Having cast the pill into the midst of water, it becomes like a diamond.
O Goddess of the Gods, having squeezed out the excellent juice of the Śāka tree and mixing it with red sandalwood, one should digest all metals. (Rasārṇava 12.172)
By means of the scent of sulphur (gandhapāṣāṇa), one should apply it to iron;
all metals will then unite and melt like water. (Rasāyana 12.173)
Gandhaka, rasaka, tāpya, mercury, and red sandalwood, combined with the juice of rudantī, cause silver to become gold. (Rasārṇava 12.174)
One should strain the resin of the *śāka* tree through its own leaf, and then grind the powder of *śigru* root with that juice. (Rasāyana 12.175)
Having smeared copper leaves and placed them in a crucible, one should cook them;
that molten substance will become divine gold, endowed with all auspicious characteristics. (Rasārṇava 12.176)
A wise person should collect the fully ripened fruits of the śāka tree and infuse them with its juice for seven nights. (Rasāyana 12.177)
One should coat the silver leaves with that juice, mixed with mañjiṣṭhā; when heated, it becomes gold. (Rasārṇava 12.178)
Next, I shall describe the procedure for the great medicinal herb *devadālī*:
it is white for the destruction of diseases, and black or yellow for the practice of *rasāyana*. (Ras 12.179)

On the full moon day, on the thirteenth day, when the sun is eclipsed by Rāhu, or else on the fifth day of the dark fortnight, one should extract this [substance] according to the prescribed rule. (Rasārṇava 12.180)
O Goddess, the fruit of *devadālī*, *viṣṇukrāntā*, and *sūtaka* cause [the mercury] to faint and bind it quickly, and they turn copper into gold. (Rasārṇava 12.181)
Having ground the fruit and root of *devadālī* together with the juice of *īśvarī* in water, one causes tin to solidify in an instant. (Rasārṇava 12.182)
Henceforth, O beloved, I shall explain the procedure for white *guñjā*. (Rasārṇava 12.183)
On the fourteenth or eighth day of the dark fortnight, O worshiper of the gods, one should place earth in a skull and sprinkle it with water. (Rasāyana 12.184)
One should sow the seeds of white guñjā together with flowers, and likewise perform the collection [of the powder] with the mantra that will be described hereafter. (Ras 12.185)

Homage to the Blessed One, the White Creeper, dweller on the White Mountain; perform, perform all tasks, O Unobstructed One! Homage, homage, svāhā! By this mantra as proclaimed, success is attained and not otherwise.
For six months, one should protect the creeper purified by the mantra. (Rasāyana 12.186)
Having taken pure copper weighing three or five palas, placed it inside a crucible, [one should treat it] with half a karṣa of white guñjā. Ras_12.187
When mercury is combined in one place with that which is devoid of odor,
and mixed together with powdered *guñjā* according to the method of Brahmā,
O Goddess, it becomes beautiful gold, the ornament of the gods. (Rasārṇava 12.188)
O Queen of the Gods, I shall explain the binding of mercury by means of "moon-water. (Rasārṇava 12.189)
On the full moon day of the bright fortnight, having seen the orb of the full moon,
the waters of the moon emerge in many ways, piercing through the earth.
Some have the color of clay and are salty in taste;
some are like the moon, and some possess the luster of the sky.
They increase with the waxing of the moon and diminish with its waning. (Rasārṇava 12.191)
Having seen the "moon-water" (candrodaka), especially on the full moon day,
the practitioner of mantra [sees it] emerge from the earth and increase in proportion to the waxing of the moon.
Having first established the boundary of the sacred field (*kṣetrabandha*) and worshipped the god Śaṅkara,
the wise practitioner, having honored that field on the fourteenth day and fasted for a full day and night, should offer an oblation (*bali*) there. (Ras 12.193)

Having gone near it on the night of the full moon, one should collect the "moon-water" (candrodaka), well-consecrated with mantras; then, having stirred it with honey and clarified butter, one should drink it with a concentrated mind. (Rasāyana 12.194)
By the mere act of drinking that very [substance], fainting occurs at that very moment.
Then, when the rising of the moon is seen, one should cause milk to be given to him.
Through its application for seven nights, he becomes as stainless as the moon. (Rasārṇava 12.195)
By using it for twenty-one nights, one may live for three days of Brahmā;
by using it for one month, that man shall attain the lifespan of Brahmā.
One should grind mercury, gold, and *candrodaka* together;
when placed inside a crucible and heated, it instantly becomes a pill. (Rasārṇava 12.197)
And by mere touch, this [substance] will transmute the eight types of metals. (Rasārṇava 12.198)

The mercury should be processed with its own juice, smelted with vajra, and added to the mass at sixty-fourth parts; however, when the mass is doubled, it is added at one-thousandth parts. (Rasāyana 12.199)
A person who places in their mouth a dose of mercury measuring one *guñjā*—bound with ten *saṃkalikās* and encased in three metals—shall attain invisibility. (Rasārṇava 12.200)

Oṃ, salutation to Rudra, whose fangs are formidable, the destroyer of obstacles; protect, protect the cardinal directions! Protect, protect the intermediate directions! Rudra commands: huṃ phaṭ svāhā!
Oṃ, salutation to the Blessed One, Rudra, who holds a trident in his hand, born from the nectar of immortality; protect, protect! phaṭ svāhā!
Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the binding of the essence of the scissors (kartarī). (Rasārṇava 12.201)
When the Asuras were assembled together, the enemy of Mura, with a mind possessed by wrath,
hurled the great Sudarśana discus.
Then, drops of sweat fell from his forehead;
having fallen upon the ground, those divine drops turned into the essence of the *kartarī* plant.
And there, the Sudarśana was established by Viṣṇu for the sake of protection;
revolving like a wheel, it cuts down all weapons.
It produces thundering roars and emits smoke and flames;
by the mere sight of it, the *kartarī* [is neutralized], as is another known as the *śabdakartarī*.
She is the scissor of touch, the scissor of shadow, and the scissor of smoke;
she is indeed the scissor of flame, the power that is the scissor of the Terrible One.
For the sake of the welfare of the worlds, she stands established as a terrible power;
having the form of essence, she is most fearsome and the cutter-off of those who have not attained accomplishment.
When he goes to her field, he should then recite the Aghora-weapon mantra;
then the wise one should again place the Ghora [mantra] there and subsequently install the Weapon [mantra]. (Ras 12.208)
Having established the *kartarī* [knife] upon the body in both direct and reverse order, one should seal it with the *mudrā* joined with the *aghorāstra* mantra. (Rasārṇava 12.209)
One should worship her with a lamp and paralyze her with incense;
then, by means of the *viṣṭarā* mudrā, one should employ the yoga of placement.
A bezoar, a stone, a maiden, a thunderbolt-root, the blood of a woman, and cow urine—this forehead mark (tilaka) brings all under one's control. (Ras 12.211)
Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the binding of mercury with poison.
Poison-water is equal to poison, and ghee-water is like ghee;
O Goddess, it is rich with colors such as white and yellow, and possesses the most excellent of tastes.
Having gone there to a forest region, one should recite the *Ghorasahasraka*;
when the hair is thrown [there], it bursts apart, and one's own shadow is not seen.
The oil becomes globular in shape and the clarified butter spreads out;
it removes the odor of sulfur, and a salty-sour taste is produced. (Rasārṇava 12.215)
Having obtained [the ingredients], one should place them in a bitter gourd using a leaf of the *pālāśa* tree;
[one should add] poison-water, sulfur, and an equal amount of *harabīja*. (Rasāyana 12.216)
Having ground copper leaves with goat’s milk, one should coat them;
then, O Goddess of Gods, by means of a *puṭa* [firing], it becomes like vermilion in color. O Goddess of Gods, with even a hundredth part of this, one may transmute all metals. (Rasārṇava 12.217)
O Goddess, by this method, the nāga attains the state of vermilion;
one should cause the piercing of that very substance with a thousandth part [of mercury]. (Rasārṇava 12.218)
Red, yellow, and likewise black produce effects in progressively increasing degrees. (Rasāyana 12.219)
Having taken three palas [of the substance] in either an iron vessel or a vessel made of gourd,
one should wrap it on the outside with *pālāśa* leaves as before.
One should place it upon a heap of grain for twenty-one days, and then one should prepare a single drop in the midst of buffalo milk. (Rasārṇava 12.221)

O Goddess, whoever should consume milk-rice mixed with honey and clarified butter, for as many palas of powder as there are grains [of rice], he shall live for that same number of years. (Rasāyana 12.222)
Lāṅgalī, soot from a house, vermilion, the two types of turmeric, meṣaśṛṅgī, śṛṅgī, kṛṣṇonmatta, and māraka; 12.223.1.
The wise one should take the seed-containing mercury and grind it with poisonous water;
he should then saturate it with poisonous water seven times.
Alternatively, one should continue to process that [substance] until it becomes a powder;
having mixed mercury with that [powder] in a sixteenfold proportion, it will come into being. (Rasārṇava 12.224)
One should also saturate it three times in a crucible known as a *mūṣā* and in a bamboo tube;
one must avoid its smoke, which greatly causes diseases of the limbs. (Rasārṇava 12.225)
Then, one should place nāgasindūra in a vessel made of gourd;
subsequently, one should pierce silver leaves with a hundredth part of that powder. (Rasārṇava 12.226)
Taking poison and water, one should prepare auspicious barley gruel; when poured into that mold, it becomes a beautiful silver [image]. (Rasāyana 12.227)
Taking poison and water, one should cast them into the best of juices;
[along with] realgar, sulphur, poison, borax, and lāṅgalī. (Rasāyana 12.228)
One should grind [the ingredients] into a fine paste in a mortar and smear it onto silver leaves;
when heated in a sealed crucible (andhamūṣā), it becomes seedless gold.
Oṃ śrīnīlakaṇṭhāya ṭha ṭhaḥ. One should recite this ten thousand times. I shall now describe the procedure for poisonous grass; listen with a concentrated mind. (Ras 12.229)
Gandha, mākṣika, and darada, combined with kunaṭī and mercury, together with viṣatṛṇa, should be rubbed with the acid juice of mātuluṅga. (Rasārṇava 12.230)
Make an ointment with one *pala* of this medicinal paste;
then, apply a *puṭa* [sealing] three times over the beautiful gold in the resinous exudate. (Rasāyana 12.231)
Now, O Pārvatī, I shall describe the procedure for the water of Saṃjīvanī. (Rasārṇava 12.232)
O Goddess, O you who are praised by the gods, in former times I was propitiated by Śukra for the sake of the benefit of the Dānavas who had died in battle with the gods. (Ras 12.233)
I bestowed upon him the Saṃjīvanī lore in the form of water;
by it, those Daityas who had died in the battle with the gods were restored to life.
I shall explain to you correctly that which has been deposited in the world of mortals. (Ras 12.235)
In the mortal world, there is a highly meritorious and purifying river named Godāvarī in the southern region, as famous as the Gaṅgā. (Ras 12.236)
And on its southern bank is the supreme city of Kadalīnagara;
to the south of that is a mountain renowned throughout all the worlds.
Known by the name Kṛṣṇagiri, it is seen as the source of all auspiciousness;
in its vicinity there is a village named Suprasiddhāmbikā. (Ras 12.238)
Even there, having observed the water, it should be examined in a place honored by the gods.
Taking a dry bamboo stalk, one should throw it into the middle of water;
within a day and night, it certainly becomes green and glossy.
It sheds sprouts and leaves, appearing truly enchanting. (Ras 12.240)
Then, one should worship the Goddess with offerings of oblations and flowers, as well as the Lord of the Field (Kṣetrādhipa), Gaṇeśa, and Caṇḍayonīśvara. (Ras 12.241)
I shall proclaim its mantra, which is difficult to obtain in the three worlds.
Oṃ, to Caṇḍa, the wielder of the Pināka bow, the one with a trident in hand: Oṃ, bind the cardinal directions, bind the intermediate directions, ṭhaṭhaḥ!
Having consecrated sesame seeds, rice grains, and mustard seeds seven times with this mantra, the practitioner should scatter them in all directions. (Ras 12.243)
Having taken water from a bitter gourd while remaining composed and having performed the protection ritual, one should diligently return to one's own place. (Ras 12.244)
Oṃ, homage to the Immortal One, whose form is nectar! Make me immortal, make me immortal! Thus Rudra commands, svāhā!
Having consecrated that water seven times with this mantra, one should likewise take mercury for one day, combined with two māṣas of gold.
The wise one should rub [the powder] with that water and drink it. (Rasāyana 12.245)
Then, by consuming milk as food with diligence for twenty-one nights,
one may live for more than ten thousand aeons, able to assume any form at will and possessed of great strength.
Having traveled a hundred yojanas, he returns once again;
invincible to all beings, that sky-walker moves according to his own will.
One should combine gold, mercury, and *vyoma* (mica) in equal parts in one place; one should grind them with that liquid and then subject them to heating (*sveda*) seven times. Ras_12.248 //
That mercury shall penetrate all metals by means of a sixtyfold part.
Alternatively, one should consume that divine elixir together with honey;
by using it for just one month, one may live for ten thousand Brahma-days.
Through its urine, excrement, and sweat, copper becomes gold.
Having taken water in a windless place, one should drink three handfuls;
immediately upon drinking it, fainting will occur, and health shall be restored within three praharas. (Rasāyana 12.252)
Thus, for twenty-one days he should subsist on milk alone;
thereafter, he becomes wise, capable of assuming any form at will, possessed of great strength, and appearing like one eight years of age. (Rasārṇava 12.253)
One who sees the entire earth with its fissures and its seven netherworlds becomes invulnerable to gods and daityas and is born with a lifespan lasting for a kalpa. (Rasārṇava 12.254)
Alternatively, taking water, mercury, and realgar, one should grind them on a grinding stone until they become a lost-paste (naṣṭapiṣṭa). // Ras_12.255 //
One should subject it to sweating for seven nights and encase it with the three metals.
One may vanish in an instant and become a lord of the Vidyādharas, surrounded by hundreds of Siddha maidens for as long as fourteen kalpas. (Rasārṇava 12.257)
During all those days, one should give rice cooked with śāli grains, along with ghee and milk; in this manner, one should perform it daily. (Ras 12.258)
I shall explain the procedure for warm water; listen with a concentrated mind.
One should observe where the warm water is found and make one's dwelling right there. (Ras 12.259)
There is a river named Godāvarī, highly renowned in Mahārāṣṭra;
on its northern side lies the Sahya mountain, a sacred peak.
There, O Goddess, is the well-known temple of the deity named Mātāpura;
to the north of that is the supreme city called Kampā.
There resides the deity Kampeśvara, and there is certainly hot water.
Having bathed there in the river named Praṇītā, the best of practitioners should thereafter perform the ritual in the pool of hot water according to the prescribed injunctions.
Having stayed there for one night, if one possessing wealth consumes [the substance] day after day for only a month, he shall live for eight hundred years. (Rasārṇava 12.263)
If one employs it for one year, he shall live happily for ten thousand years;
freed from wrinkles and grey hair, he becomes an enjoyer of pleasures like Indra himself. (Rasāyana 12.264)
If one drinks water for one year, he may live as long as the moon, sun, and stars;
by his urine and feces, copper becomes gold. (Rasārṇava 12.265)
One should add hot water, ferrous sulfate (kāsīsa), and sulfur combined with an equal portion of antimony (rasaka) as a fourth part, along with ten parts [of the base metal]. (Ras 12.266)
One should grind all the copper until it becomes a "lost-powder" (naṣṭapiṣṭa) in an instant;
by merely being smeared with that, the copper becomes gold. (Rasārṇava 12.267)
The wise one should add a counter-impregnation with that infused water;
thus the copper becomes gold, possessing the brilliance of the rising sun. (Rasārṇava 12.268)
Gold that has been infused with its liquid and combined with the essence of the seed, and silver likewise infused by this method, shall attain the state of gold.
One should consume *bhallātaka* with warm water and sesame paste;
by practicing this for two months, one shall live for three hundred years. (Rasāyana 12.270)
One should rub together realgar, sulphur, green vitriol, blue vitriol, cinnabar,
and pyrite with hot water for one watch (yāma), and then smear the resulting paste onto silver leaves.
O Goddess, by blowing [the fire] twice, it becomes fourteen-colored;
O Mistress of the Gods, by this sequence, the copper becomes sixteen-colored. (Rasārṇava 12.272)

Having separately rubbed one part each of gold and silver with two parts of *kāntaloha* and iron ore using hot water, it attains the state of a solid bolus (*khoṭa*) through heating. (Rasārṇava 12.273)
One should hold it in the mouth for a month, and the person shall become one with a vajra-body.

One should consume that powder, the size of a barley grain, with honey and clarified butter; when it reaches the weight of one pala, copper is transformed into gold by its impurities. (Rasārṇava 12.274)
One should eat horse gram cooked in hot water and subsist on milk;
by bathing with warm water for year after year, one shall live for a hundred years. (Rasāyana 12.275)
One should cook milk, warm water, and a decoction of *triphalā* together in a vessel made of *kānta* iron; having prepared this *pāyasa*, one should consume it for one month.
By eating this, a man shall live for a hundred kalpas and attain the lifespan of Viṣṇu. (Rasārṇava 12.276)
Henceforth, O beloved, I shall explain the procedure for mountain-water (śailodaka), which is of four kinds: mud-water (kardamāpa), earth-mountain (mahīśaila), and stone (śila). (Rasārṇava 12.277)
Some [medicines] on this earth pierce in a single moment, some pierce in a day, while others pierce in a fortnight, a month, or up to six months. (Rasārṇava 12.278)

O Goddess of the Gods, when the wood has been cast [into the crucible] and is seen to have become like stone, both externally and internally, that is proclaimed as "piercing" (vedhaka). (Rasārṇava 12.279)
Cinnabar, yellow orpiment, sulfur, and realgar—that which removes the odor from these is called *vedhaka*. (Rasārṇava 12.280)
One should place sulfur and talaka into a jar filled with water;
when it takes the form of bubbles, then it becomes *śailodaka*.
Otherwise, O Goddess, it is merely a coating and should not be taken, as it is useless. (Rasārṇava 12.281)
On the stone slab named Paryaṅka at the edge of the Śrīvana forest on Mount Śrīśaila,
situated there on the bank of the river Bhagavatī, it pierces in an instant;
in that same place, it pierces in a single day, but at Gokarṇa, it takes three days.
In Bhadrāṅga, the piercing of the day occurs; at the end of Tristhala, it lasts for three days;
at Dhāreśvara, it lasts for a fortnight; and in Varṣāpurī, it lasts for one day. (Ras 12.283)
At Brahmeśvara, the [observance] lasts for a month; at Vyāghrapurī, however, it is for a day.
At Aghoreśa, it is for a month, and likewise again at Siṃhadvīpa. At Brahmagiri it is for one day, but at Vindhya it is a "piercing-instant" (kṣaṇavedhaka).
In the Mālyavant mountains, there is hot water that pierces through stone in an instant.
On the delightful Kiṣkindhyā mountain, by the shore of Lake Pampā, there is grass and water;
O Goddess, two yojanas further to its west, there is a hill on the ground, and right there on that mountain, pierce it for three days. (Ras 12.286)

In the city of the Goddess on Mount Sahya, in the vicinity of Kṣīrakṣetra, Śailodaka is a "piercer of ten million" (koṭivedhin) even in a difficult region; in the city named Gokula belonging to Nṛsiṃha, it is a "piercer of a hundred thousand" (lakṣavedhin). (Rasārṇava 12.287)
Elsewhere, wherever it may be, that which arises from Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva is nectar; in each such place, there is the supreme method of vajrīkaraṇa. (Ras 12.288)
I shall explain its origin so that practitioners may understand it. (Rasārṇava 12.289)
From the body of the Boar who lifted up the earth,
the sweat that fell from it gave rise to the supreme Śailodaka.
If [the mark] appears on its face, it lasts for a moment; on the chest, for a day;
by the two arms, it persists for three days; on the sides, it lasts for a month; and on the other parts of the body, for six months; in all these cases, the result is equal. (Ras 12.291)
Having performed the protection of that sacred field with the Aghora weapon and having offered the bali-oblation to the directions,
one should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times and then take up the supreme nectar.
O worshipper of the gods, during autumn, summer, spring, or winter,
one should place eight palas of iron, copper, or a gourd vessel, along with a pala of milk, into a vessel made of stone, water, or clay. (Rasāyana 12.293)
Having boiled it until only the milk remains, a person should drink it for twenty-one days;
he shall live for a thousand years, free from wrinkles and grey hair. (Rasāyana 12.294)
Alternatively, one may consume eight palas of milk mixed with one pala of water;
when only the milk remains, one should partake of it and obtain the aforementioned fruit. (Rasāyana 12.295)
One should boil water eight times the quantity of horse gram (kulattha) until one-eighth remains;
with that decoction, which is four times the amount of ghee, one should cook the clarified butter until only the ghee remains. (Rasakalpa 12.296)
One should lick [it] mixed with honey for three weeks, O Goddess; having understood the strength and weakness of the scriptures, Bṛhaspati attained mastery over them in a month.
He will have the appearance of a sixteen-year-old and live for a thousand years, without a doubt. (Rasāyana 12.297)

One should eat the remaining kulattha beans mixed with honey and ghee in a quantity equal to one-fourth [of the previous dose] for one year; by this, one lives for ten thousand years. (Rasāyana 12.298)
One should perform anointing and massage with the oil prepared from that; by massaging for one month, it brings about the perfection of the body. (Rasāyana 12.299)
One shall suddenly conquer scabies, eczema, ringworm, and leprosy;
freed from wrinkles and graying hair, one attains a lifespan of a thousand years. (Rasāyana 12.300)
Whoever, having risen in the morning, drinks three handfuls of mountain water, shall live for a thousand years, free from wrinkles and grey hair, within six months. (Rasāyana 12.301)
Alternatively, O Goddess, one should grind the *sūtaka* with water;
within one month, O Mistress of the Gods, it will become a "lost-powder" (*naṣṭapiṣṭa*).
If one should consume it for only a month, he would become free from old age and death.
Alternatively, that mercury should be rubbed with gold to produce gold ash; then, being strong, one should melt it with that liquid using a fire of khadira wood. (Rasārṇava 12.304)
The pill named Sundarī wards off all weapons;
its maker, having attained self-perfection, shall live as long as the moon, sun, and stars. (Rasāyana 12.305)
Realgar, mica, iron pyrite, gold, and likewise silver—all of these should be cooked with milk and wine for three days.
By using this for only a month, one becomes free from wrinkles and grey hair. (Rasārṇava 12.306)
Then, one should cook milk-rice (pāyasa) with half as much milk using that very water;
by practicing this for just one month, wrinkles and grey hair are destroyed. (Rasāyana 12.307)
Having cooked sixty-three hundred pathyā fruits with that water and having mixed in honey, one should place the entire quantity in a vessel and set it in the ground.
Having risen in the morning, one should likewise eat one [pill] each day;
thus freed from wrinkles and graying hair, one shall live for a thousand years. (Rasāyana 12.309)
One may eat horse gram that has been turned into a solid mass with honey and clarified butter;
by consuming it for six months, one may live for a thousand years. (Rasāyana 12.310)
