Having killed the *kūṣmāṇḍa* [plant] and whatever other fruits there may be, one should eat them along with iron cast into water that has become solidified like stone; by subsisting on a diet of milk until the end of digestion, a man becomes possessed of a vajra-body. (Rasārṇava 12.311)
O Dear One, having kneaded the mica with that water, one should boil it;
by consuming it combined with the three pungents (kaṭutraya), one shall live for a thousand years. (Rasārṇava 12.312)

Alternatively, one should grind one karṣa of the mercury with water, place it inside the pulp of an iṅgudī fruit, and submerge that within mountain water; after exactly three times that duration, its hardness arises. (Rasārṇava 12.313)
If it is held in the mouth for six months, it makes one's body vajra-like; possessing strength equal to ten elephants, one rejoices together with the gods. (Rasāyana 12.314)
Having taken triphalā, one should throw it into that mountain water;
when that [water] has become solidified as stone, one should take it and grind it into powder. (Rasāyana 12.315)
One should consume well-digested mercury together with that [elixir], saturated with ghee and honey, for one year; thereafter, one should subsist on milk alone.
Resembling the rising sun, intelligent, and pleasing to behold,
with dark and curly hair, he shall live as long as the moon, the sun, and the stars.
One should combine together mercury, yellow orpiment, realgar, pyrite, cinnabar, and poison. (Rasārṇava 12.318)
One should grind it on a grinding stone with the juice of *mātuluṅga*;
having formed it into a pill, one should place it in the middle of water. (Rasārṇava 12.319)
By that, silver and copper certainly become gold. (Rasāyana 12.320)
If one uses it for one month, one becomes free from wrinkles and grey hair;
such a person will live for a thousand years, endowed with great strength and prowess.
By merely adding the powder of that [mercury] to turmeric that has been turned into stone, the lead attains the state of gold, possessing a luster like the rising sun. (Rasārṇava 12.322)
Having cast it into mountain water, or onto the earth, a rock, or even into mud,
one should then bind the mercury once the appropriate duration of time has been determined.
Gold that has been smelted with red alkali and amalgamated in equal parts acts as a gold-maker for all metals when used at a one-hundredth part [of their weight]. (Rasārṇava 12.324)
Having attained the second stage of refinement, one should consume it with honey and clarified butter;
at that time, the wind (vital energy) arises above those [impurities] born of the mind. (Rasāyana 12.325)
He shall possess knowledge of the time [of death] and live for fifty thousand years.
Having attained the second stage of sublimation (*sāraṇā*), one pierces it with a thousandth part [of mercury];
by holding that *khoṭa* in the mouth, one certainly attains divinity. (Rasārṇava 12.327)
In *nicula*, *kakubha*, *kiṃśuka*, or even *madhuka*;
or within the pulp of the *iṅgudī* fruit, or from the midst of the two types of *rajanī*. (Rasāyana 12.328)
One should grind mercury and sulfur into the form of pills;
having wrapped them in gold, one should cook them for one day and then wear them. (Rasārṇava 12.329)
Having carefully enveloped it with a paste of triphalā and vyoṣa, and having added a quarter part of gold, one should then join mercury to it;
if one places it in the midst of mountain water, the pill will become like a diamond. (Rasārṇava 12.330)
The process of *sāraṇā* should be performed as before; it will grant success as before. When held in the mouth, however, it bestows a lifespan of a thousand years. (Rasārṇava 12.331)
Through the second application of *sāraṇā*, it should pierce ten thousand [times];
when held in the mouth, this very [substance] bestows a lifespan of ten thousand years. (Rasārṇava 12.332)
Through the third application of sublimation (*sāraṇā*), it becomes capable of hitting a target at a distance of one hundred thousand;
if one holds that pill (*khoṭa*) in the mouth, the man attains a lifespan of one hundred thousand years. (Rasārṇava 12.333)
Having attained the fourth stage of refinement (*sāraṇā*), there is no doubt that the piercing of ten million (*koṭivedha*) occurs;
his lifespan becomes ten million years, and he attains the power of moving through the sky (*khecaratva*). (Rasārṇava 12.334)
With five [units] there would be ten crores; with six, there would be one hundred crores;
until the lifespan of the sun and moon, he possesses infinite strength and vigor.
That other pill, known as Sāraṇā, also bestows the seventh [power];
it is renowned as Khecarī and was impelled by Bhairava. (Rasārṇava 12.336)
But he who should consume even a single *rājikā* seed for one month shall become a perfected one (*siddha*) with a body of adamant (*vajradeha*), beloved by divine women;
he sports at will with the enjoyments of sky-farers and shall attain the state of Śiva. (Ras 12.337)
Various kinds of fruits may also arise from the seed-oils of those [plants] along with their juices; and mercury bound by that—listen, O beautiful one, to the method for the pill. (Rasārṇava 12.338)
One should cause mercury, purified and bound, to digest sulfur therein;
once three times the amount of sulfur has been digested, one should then prepare gold with it. (Rasāyana 12.339)
One should cause the mercury to be reduced to ash; therein, the mercury is gold.
That ash should be digested within the mercury, equal in measure to the lord of mercury (rasendra). (Rasārṇava 12.340)
By means of that digested *sūtaka*, one should digest *vajraratna*;
that *vajra* becomes an ash resembling the redness of vermilion. (Rasārṇava 12.341)
One should digest that ash within mercury that has been tripled and honored with liquor;
then one should extract it into gold and fashion a pill from it. (Rasārṇava 12.342)
Having cast that [pill], encased in three metals, into his mouth, the practitioner becomes devoid of shadow; he thus becomes invisible even to gods and dānavas. (Rasārṇava 12.343)
O Goddess, at that very moment one should pierce all metals with gold;
for many thousands of years one shall remain free from wrinkles and grey hair. (Rasārṇava 12.344)
One should wear a trident joined with a spear, adorned with the qualities of jewels and so forth,
upon the mouth and the hand, for the purpose of warding off all weapons.
Sky, the essence of *mākṣika*, pure silver, the weapon of the gods (*surāyudha*), *vaikrānta*, *tālaka*, mercury, and gems adorned with excellent qualities; *Rasārṇava* 12.346.
O lady of excellent hips, that pill, when combined with the three sweets and held in the mouth, will directly destroy grey hair; of this there is no doubt.
O Queen of the Gods, it is like Śiva and Śakti, or like the gems and other [ornaments] belonging to Śiva. (Rasārṇava 12.347)
One should prepare equal parts of gold, silver, and mercury;
then, having placed the woman's menses within a tiger-skin, one should wrap it with a lotus fiber. (Rasārṇava 12.348)
One should sprinkle that [substance], wrap it accordingly, and place it in a secret location;
victory will be achieved in battle, in the royal court, in gambling, in divine rites, or in matters of desire.
Furthermore, whoever places that ball in his mouth shall become a charmer of all. (Rasārṇava 12.349)
Vaikrānta, abhraka, kānta, sasyaka, and surāyudha should be equal in measure to the kāñcika produced from vibhītaka and other such sources. (Rasārṇava 12.350)

Then one should produce rājāvarta and apply it by means of a foot-paste. A single auspicious pill, rubbed with the juice of kumārī, destroys disease, death, and old age when held in the mouth; of this there is no doubt. (Rasāyana 12.351)
O lady of beautiful hips, there are five stars, two *sūtakas*, and three parts of the sky (*ākāśa*), with one part each for gold and mercury. (Rasārṇava 12.352)

O Arasundarī, by means of the half-mercury procedure, one becomes a pill; by holding it in the mouth, one becomes indeed inexhaustible, free from old age, possessed of great strength, liberated from all diseases, and shall live [long]. (Rasārṇava 12.353)
One *pala* of ash-mercury (*bhasmasūta*), likewise one *pala* of dead magnetite (*mṛtakānta*), one *pala* of honey (*mākṣika*), and furthermore one *pala* of bitumen (*śilājatu*). (Rasārṇava 12.354)
One pala of viḍaṅga and one pala of powdered pathyā, having combined all of this together, one should then grind it with honey and ghee. (Rasakalpa 12.355)
O Goddess, one should have three hundred and sixty pills prepared;
one should consume them daily, continuously for one year. (Ras 12.356)
Possessing great strength and equal to Rudra, he shall live for thousands of years.
Hereafter, I shall explain the elixir of mercury-ash (rasabhasma-rasāyana), which is to be known as free from contraindications and is truly a supreme, divine medicine. (Rasārṇava 12.358)
One should roast mercury (pārada) together with āmalakī and other ingredients, kānta iron, and realgar (manaḥśilā),
along with seven parts of vākucī, ground with the juice of milky trees (kṣīriṇī) and combined with the juice of meghanāda, inside a "dumb" crucible (mūkamūṣā). (Rasārṇava 12.359)

One should consume one *māṣa*, then three *māṣas*, and then triple that amount in sequence; O Goddess, after three years, [the dose] gradually becomes one-quarter and half a *niṣka* respectively. (Rasāyana 12.360)
For six, seven, and eight years respectively, according to the measure of the niṣka,
he shall enjoy divine food, free from old age and deformity.
Whoever consumes a *niṣka* or even half a *niṣka* of this [substance] combined with a small amount of gold will, within three years, fully conquer all diseases. (Rasāyana 12.362)
At eight years of age he has a lifespan of a thousand years; at twelve, he is a piercer of a hundred thousand targets;
and at sixteen years, O Goddess, he becomes possessed of a divine form. (Rasārṇava 12.363)

One hundred palas of *abhayā* and the same amount of *akṣadhātrī* are boiled in eight hundred parts of water until one-eighth remains; this decoction, enriched with ghee, honey, and sugar, along with a tenth part of the three pungents (*vyoṣa*) and *citraka*, is processed with meat juice and fruit juice, and combined with iron that has been digested and calcined. (Rasakalpa 12.364)
Viḍaṅga, equal in measure to girija and abhra, with beautiful bees (kānta-bhṛṅga), well-matured together with mercury, along with the finest divine rice;
this paste, prepared for three days by gentle heating in an iron vessel, is the most excellent. (Rasārṇava 12.365)

At the time of lying down, he who frequents the left eye, possessing a waist as firm and dense as a cloud, with the pride of an elephant in rut, free from all defects, with divine vision in every direction, and with beauty like that of Madana, is the preeminent hero among women. (Ras 12.366)
With a body like a water-lily bud and dark, curly hair, he is pure like the preceptor of the gods, a true poet, and a creator of wonders;
with the gait and movements of a bull and a voice that is smooth and deep, he is like the celestial elephant in this world, constantly and swiftly destroying the weariness of all.

Indeed, there flourishes in this world one who lives by the moon, stars, and sun; who possesses the exquisite beauty of the lotus-dwelling goddess; who is a knower of the treatises on logic and other sciences; who is a protector of the conventions of the virtuous; who is initiated into the Dharma; who is as profound as Hari, Hara, and the Goddess; and who is as steadfast as the sun, the moon, and the ocean. (Ras 12.368)

Antimony, gold, copper, and moonstone (mica), along with *iṅgudī* fruit, form a beautiful pill (*golaka*) containing the essence of mountains, waters, and perfected beings; it is auspicious and delights even the immortals. (Rasāyana 12.369)
Antimony, gold, copper, and silver, mica, the diamond-gem, and a pellet of the king of serpents, when cast into the hollow of an *āmalaka* wood and buried in the earth or a mountain, are extracted;
having attained the state of stone, when placed in the mouth, they produce a diamond-like body within a few days. (Rasārṇava 12.370)

A pill made from *tāla*, excellent gold, copper, and mercury, bound within a wooden frame using a ball of wood, and containing the beautiful essence of *śailavāri* (rock-water), is called the *khecarī* pill. (Rasārṇava 12.371)
One should eat palāśa seeds that have been cast into mountain water and processed with honey and ghee;
by doing so for twenty-one days, taking it once every day, a man shall live for a thousand years and be victorious. (Rasāyana 12.372)
Sūtaka and abhraka, combined with the milk of the Vajrī plant and joined with gold, shall become the Khecarī pill. (Rasārṇava 12.373)
One should place mercury within the interior of a *karañja* fruit;
situated in the midst of a mountain of ghee and water, it bestows a lifespan of a thousand years. (Rasārṇava 12.374)
In *tinduka* [oil], the lifespan is two thousand years; in *jambīra*, three thousand;
and in *mātuluṅga* and *nāraṅga*, four and five thousand years respectively. (Rasāyana 12.375)
Six thousand [seeds] are found in the fruit of the *rambhā* plantain, seven in number in the *panasa* jackfruit, and ten thousand in number in the fruit of the *vibhītaka*. (Ras 12.376)
In a coconut, O noble lady, there are fourteen thousand;
in a lotus, thirty thousand; and furthermore, in an āmalaka fruit, one hundred thousand. (Ras 12.377)
One should boil mercury in the liquid of mica-leaf for a day and night in water containing realgar;
the mercury extracted from that destroys death and poverty. (Rasārṇava 12.378)
Through the application of the process of *sāraṇā*, a new body is born;
in both mercury and elixir (*rasāyana*), it undoubtedly becomes capable of piercing a hundred thousand targets.
Having formed a pill from the mud and the essence of a maiden, a person should hold that which falls from the mouth through heating;
by practicing this for six months, one indeed attains freedom from old age and immortality. (Rasārṇava 12.380)
One should smelt antimony combined with mercury and mixed with quicksilver;
by holding that solidified mass (khoṭa) in the mouth, one certainly becomes invisible. (Rasāyana 12.381)
Whatever procedure for water is prescribed in the Śiva-āgama, one should indeed perform that elixir (rasāyana) at the proper time using that very essence. (Ras 12.382)
